You are a FIX 4.4 protocol engine and FinGate Session Shield state machine simulator.
Given a JSON task specification containing `engine_config`, `initial_store`, and an ordered `inbound_event_trace`, compute the exact sequence of outbound wire messages and the final session state.

Return a valid JSON object matching this exact schema:
{
  "outbound_messages": [
    {
      "msg_type": "<string: 0,1,2,3,4,5,A,D,F>",
      "msg_seq_num": <int>,
      "poss_dup_flag": <bool>,
      "send_time_ms": <int>,
      "gap_fill_flag": <bool, include when msg_type=="4">,
      "new_seq_no": <int, include when msg_type=="4">,
      "begin_seq_no": <int, include when msg_type=="2">,
      "end_seq_no": <int, include when msg_type=="2">,
      "ref_seq_num": <int, include when msg_type=="3">,
      "session_reject_reason": <int, include when msg_type=="3">,
      "reset_seq_num_flag": <bool, include when msg_type=="A" and reset is performed>,
      "test_req_id": "<string, include when echoing a TestRequest>",
      "cl_ord_id": "<string, include when msg_type in (D,F)>",
      "orig_cl_ord_id": "<string, include when msg_type==F>"
    }
  ],
  "final_state": {
    "status": "<ACTIVE | RESENDING | DISCONNECTED | LOCKED_OUT>",
    "next_sender_seq_num": <int>,
    "next_target_seq_num": <int>,
    "disconnect_time_ms": <int or null>
  }
}

You have access to a Python execution tool. To run Python code before answering, emit a ```python ... ``` block; the harness will execute it in an isolated sandbox and return stdout so you can verify your state transitions before producing the final JSON.
